The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=0, so P4(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)2!x2+f‴(0)3!x3+f(4)(0)4!x4.

So we need to work out f(0), f′(0), f″(0), f‴(0) and f(4)(0), as follows: f(x)=(1+x)3/2⟹f(0)=(1)3/2=1f′(x)=32(1+x)1/2⟹f′(0)=32f″(x)=34(1+x)−1/2⟹f″(0)=34f‴(x)=−38(1+x)−3/2⟹f‴(0)=−38f(4)(x)=916(1+x)−5/2⟹f(4)(0)=916

Therefore, P4(x) is given by P4(x)=1+(32)⋅x+(34)2!x2+(−38)3!x3+(916)4!x4=1+32x+38x2−116x3+3128x4.

Your Answer:
38x2+116x3
